answer: Capacity-capped trust graphs deter Sybil attacks in agent markets trading ocean data or umber pigments. Root anchors inject finite flow through signed peer vouches, and each admitted agent consumes a set threshold of edge-disjoint flow so trust can ripple only across bounded cut edges. Attackers must earn scarce honest endorsements per identity rather than branching behind one compromised link. However, isolated newcomers face cold-start exclusion, and colluding anchors can skew flow.
